title: AIDA implementation baseline
description: What was already broken at the commit the build starts from, at <task folder>/implementation/baseline.json (ideal/implementation.md, 'The deciding checks run before anything judges'). Taken once, by the same `preconditions` step that resolves the recipes, and only when that run's own verdict permits the build to continue: a baseline taken after a condition answered no would measure a broken environment. Every deciding check later in the stage excludes this file's own findings from its own verdict, because a repository with one pre-existing failure would otherwise block every work order forever. Recording a red suite here changes nothing about that recording run's own verdict or exit code; knowing it is the whole point. Plain JSON, no fences, no markdown. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other AIDA record carries.

takenAt.description: The UTC date the baseline ran, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script, never typed. Kept for the same reason preconditions.json keeps one: a person reading this weeks later needs to know how old it is, because a repository changes.

commit.description: The commit this baseline was taken at, read from the ledger's own startedFrom rather than a fresh git call, so the two records that must agree are read from the same place (ledger-schema.json, startedFrom). A baseline is taken once per commit: a second preconditions run whose ledger started from this same commit leaves this file alone, and a run whose ledger started from a different commit refuses rather than overwrite it, naming both commits.

scope.description: The union of every work order's own ownedFiles from the snapshot, sorted once with duplicates removed. Recorded even though nothing here reads it yet: it is what codingStandards, staticAnalysis and security will scope to once a recipe names a tool for one of them. suite is never scoped by it, because at this point the orders' own tests do not exist yet and no framework declares a command mapping paths to the tests that cover them.

suite.description: One entry per framework the project declares, running that framework's own `suite` test-command row whole and unscoped, exactly as preconditions.json already resolved and recorded it. A project on two frameworks gets two runs, because the build runs in one repository that is both.

codingStandards.description: What the coding-standards tool found across the scope above. Always undeclared today: no recipe names a coding-standards tool at this point in the process. A real field rather than an omitted one, so a later recipe that starts naming one has somewhere to write met, unmet or unknown without this file's shape changing.

staticAnalysis.description: What static analysis found across the scope above. Always undeclared today, for the same reason codingStandards is: no recipe names a static-analysis tool at this point in the process.

security.description: What the security tool found across the scope above. Always undeclared today, for the same reason codingStandards is: no recipe names a security tool at this point in the process.

framework.description: The framework name as project.json records it, the same value preconditions.json's own frameworks[].framework carries. Joined on, never re-derived.

verdict.description: met on exit 0, unmet on any other exit the command actually returned, unknown when it could not be run at all: the recipe named no suite row, the row is one of the recipe's own absent rows, its argv did not parse, a placeholder had no supplied --value, or the command could not be found (exit 127). undeclared is not here: a whole framework declining to say how it runs its own tests at all is not a fact this stage has seen yet, and adding the word before a recipe ever needs it would be a guess.

reason.description: Why this is unknown, present only on that verdict. Free text rather than a closed set, the same convention preconditions.json's own smoke.reason follows, because one of its causes is a placeholder token no --value supplied and naming which one is the point.

exitCode.description: What the suite command exited with, present whenever it actually ran.

output.description: What the command printed, standard output and standard error together, present whenever it actually ran, met or not. Unlike preconditions.json's own smoke.output, this is kept for a met run too: a baseline is a record of the whole state at this commit, not only of what pointed at a defect, and a later comparison needs something to compare against. Trimmed to at most the last 4000 characters.

truncated.description: True when output is the trimmed tail of a longer capture, absent entirely otherwise, the same convention preconditions.json's own smoke.truncated follows.

verdict.description: The same four words every verdict in this stage uses. Only undeclared is ever written today.

reason.description: Why: today always because no recipe names a tool for this at this point in the process. Never guessed from the project and never an invented tool name.
